writeup.headline: Caris rates Hold at 64, one point below Buy, on fast growth and strong momentum offset by heavy dilution.
writeup.thesis: Caris scores 64, a Hold that sits just 1 point under the Buy line, driven mainly by its trend and growth factors. The price is at its 52-week high, 65.0% above its 200-day average, with shares 90.4 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days, giving a trend score of 88. Growth scores 74 on TTM revenue growth of 85.4% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 45.4% year on year, though growth slowed by 33.4 pp from the previous quarter. Quality holds the score back at 45: the operating margin is 15.5%, but the diluted share count is up 335.8% year on year and stock-based pay is 6.6% of revenue. Balance sheet and valuation could not be scored, though in absolute terms a P/S of 10.1x and EV/EBIT of 62.5x are high, and news risk is roughly neutral at 54, helped by October price-target raises.
key_risks: Revenue growth is decelerating sharply, slowing by 33.4 pp from the previous quarter.
Diluted share count up 335.8% year on year dilutes each shareholder's claim on earnings.
Absolute valuation is high at 10.1x sales and 62.5x EV/EBIT, leaving little room for disappointment.
The price is 23.5% above its 50-day average and at its 52-week high, so a pullback could quickly hurt the trend score.
An early-stage DOJ False Claims Act investigation and GRAIL's Galleri test advancing toward FDA approval are open threats.
what_would_change: A gain of just 1 point, such as stronger Q3 results on November 4 lifting growth or quality, would move the rating to Buy.
Easing dilution or confirmed positive free cash flow would raise the quality score.
A drop of 20 points would be needed for Sell, e.g. a sharp momentum reversal combined with a guidance cut or adverse DOJ developments.
